canonical_definition: Computational Efficiency refers to achieving comparable or superior task performance with reduced computational resources (e.g., FLOPs, memory, energy) and time (e.g., latency, training/inference duration), particularly during model deployment phases such as pretraining, finetuning, or inference. It is often operationalized through metrics like generation latency on real hardware, reduced PFLOPS*days consumption, or lower inference FLOPs per block, with some definitions emphasizing resource savings during long-context processing or on-device deployment. While some approaches prioritize token-efficient representations or eliminate computationally intensive components (e.g., fully-connected layers), others focus on balancing efficiency gains with minimal performance trade-offs (e.g., 2×–8× speed-ups with small score drops). Scope varies across sources, with certain definitions encompassing both training and inference efficiency, while others narrow focus to specific stages or hardware constraints.
